title: Holt capacity: when to migrate
description: Is the home server still big enough: headroom over days, peaks against the limits.

list.name: points_per_hour
list.label: GitHub points per hour, per token

options.content:
### When is it time to move off this server?

Look at **a week or more** (top right). One bad hour is an incident, not a reason to move.
It is time when, **on ordinary days**, any of these holds:

| Sign | Move when | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CPU busy at the daily peak | over **70%** most days | deploys build on this machine too; above that every build slows the site |
| Memory available at its lowest | under **2 GB** most days | a deploy's build may take up to 3 GB; under 1 GB the alert fires |
| CPU or memory pressure | over **10%** for an hour | work is stalling for lack of CPU or memory, whatever the averages say |
| `/` disk free | under **15%** after cleaning up | under 10% the alert fires; a build can fill the rest |
| User workers busy | all of them, for **over an hour a day** | people queue; more workers need more memory (about 50 MB each) |
| Checks per hour | over **60%** of GitHub's ceiling | that limit is GitHub's, not the server's: a bigger server won't help, more tokens will |

Red dashed lines on the charts are those limits. Raising `HOLT_JOB_CONCURRENCY` or the pool is the first step; moving is for when the machine itself is the limit.

panels.description: The highest 5-minute average over the time range, across all cores.

panels.title: Memory available, lowest
panels.description: The lowest it got over the time range.

panels.title: / disk free
panels.description: / holds Docker's images and build cache. Alert: under 10%.

panels.title: /home disk free
panels.description: /home holds the database backups, evidence snapshots and this stack's data.

panels.title: User workers busy, peak
panels.description: The most user workers busy at once, as a share of HOLT_JOB_CONCURRENCY.

panels.title: Checks per hour, peak vs GitHub
panels.description: The busiest hour's finished checks as a share of what GitHub's points allow.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Share of all cores in use. The line is the migrate threshold: 70% at the daily peak.

panels.title: Load against cores
panels.description: Load above the number of cores means work is waiting for a CPU.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: What programs can still take without swapping. Lines: 2 GB (migrate), 1 GB (alert).

panels.title: Pressure: time stalled waiting
panels.description: Share of time some work was stalled for lack of CPU, memory or disk. The clearest sign of an outgrown machine: over 10% for an hour.

panels.title: / disk: free space in two weeks at this rate
panels.description: A straight line through the last 3 days. Below zero: / fills within two weeks.

panels.title: Memory against each container's limit
panels.description: At 100% Docker kills the container. Over 90% often: raise its mem_limit (deploy/prod/compose.yml).

panels.title: CPU by container
panels.description: In cores: 1 is one core fully busy.

panels.title: User workers busy
panels.description: Peak concurrency. Busy touching the line for long means people queue.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests being answered at once (open progress streams included), and the rate.

panels.title: Checks per hour against GitHub's ceiling
panels.description: The ceiling is what GitHub's hourly points allow: points per hour per token ÷ points one check uses (the two boxes at the top of the page).

panels.description: Warm passes and people's checks together.
